title: Silverpine LLM feasibility scouting call
summary: Initial discovery with Silverpine to map requirements for a production LLM feature set. Primary drivers: document-heavy retrieval over long context, multilingual support (EN/DE/FR), and secure PII handling. Team is leaning toward starting hosted for speed but needs clear path to Dedicated/Private for compliance. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share security pack, performance benchmarks for 32k/64k contexts, quote for a 3-month POC, and schedule an engineering deep-dive to scope tool-calling connectors.
action_items: Jasmine Patel: Send security whitepaper + SOC2 report (due 2025-10-03)
Marco Ruiz: Prepare initial perf/latency estimates for 32k and 64k contexts on hosted and Dedicated (due 2025-10-06)
Markus Vogel: Share sample document corpus (~50k docs) and representative queries for evaluation (due 2025-10-02)
Priya Nair: Confirm success criteria for POC and stakeholder list (due 2025-10-07)
next_steps: Redwood to provision trial hosted keys and a sandbox project for Silverpine (Jasmine)
Schedule a 90-minute technical deep-dive with Redwood SEs to map connectors (Marco + Markus)
Silverpine to upload sample corpus to secure S3 share for benching
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Dina (CTO, Silverpine), Markus (ML Eng), Priya (Product)

Summary/Notes: initial feasibility and model selection scout; focus on long-context doc retrieval, multilingual user base, and compliance path.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jasmine: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have about 55 minutes today, thanks for making time. quick introductions from our side, I run GTM at Redwood, Marco is our solutions engineer who will cover the technical q's.
[00:18] Dina: Hi all, Dina here, CTO at Silverpine. We're evaluating open models and deployment choices.
[00:23] Markus: Markus, ML eng. I'll be hands-on with evals.
[00:27] Priya: Priya from product; interested in UX and latency tradeoffs.
[00:31] Jasmine: Awesome. Marco, you want to kick off?
[00:33] Marco: Yeah sure, thanks. So high level, today we want to understand your workload — documents, languages, typical session lengths — and then map model options and deployment (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Also cover tool-calling needs, security, and POC next steps.
[00:47] Priya: Quick context — we build a contract analytics product. Customers upload large corpora, search + summarize across many docs. Must support English, German, French. Typical session often pulls in 20–40 documents, sometimes entire contract bundles ~50k tokens. We're exploring long-context models, maybe 64k.
[01:10] Markus: And security-wise, some customers require VPC and KMS, others are fine with hosted if we can guarantee data retention controls.
[01:18] Marco: Got it. A couple clarifying q's: what's your target latency for interactive flows? and are you planning to do retrieval-augmented generation vs full ingestion and fine-tune?
[01:29] Priya: Target is sub-1.2s for short answers, but for long summaries we can accept up to 5s. Main flow is RAG; we do retrieval and then generate a consolidated summary.
[01:40] Dina: We may also need to call internal tools — a connector to our document DB and an approvals API for flagged outputs. So tool-calling support is a must.
[01:50] Marco: Understood. For model choice, there are tradeoffs: larger open models (Llama 3 variants, Mistral X, Falcon) versus smaller quantized variants that reduce cost but may impact output quality on complex summarization. For 64k contexts we typically look at models that have tested well at longer context lengths, plus we use Redwood's prefix/KV cache to reduce token costs for iterative sessions.
[02:14] Markus: How mature is long-context support — like 128k? we're not sure if we need that but want headroom.
[02:20] Marco: 128k is still emerging; very few open models do that robustly out of the box. We recommend a staged approach: start with 32k–64k profiles. We can run benchmarks on both hosted and dedicated. Dedicated gives you more control and often lower per-token cost at scale, and better isolation for compliance. But hosted is fastest to start.
[02:42] Priya: Can you clarify what isolation means? Data residency?
[02:45] Jasmine: Yeah so Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and can be configured with a private network path. Private (our VPC/on-prem option) gives you customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS integration — that's the path for strict compliance customers. Hosted keeps data in Redwood's managed infra but we have options for retention and redaction and SOC2 controls.
[03:05] Dina: Ok. On models — which ones should we test first for summarization over multi-docs and multilingual?
[03:12] Marco: I'd suggest three buckets: 1) Strong open multinlingual base like Llama 3 (if you can test variants that were finetuned), 2) Mistral / Mistral X which is competitive on instruction tasks, and 3) Falcon derivatives which are cost-effective for throughput. We can also include some 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants to compare cost/latency. For German/French support we saw Llama 3 and Mistral performing better than older Llama 2 variants.
[03:40] Markus: Any gotchas with tool-calling across Hosted vs Dedicated?
[03:44] Marco: Tool-calling itself is supported in all modes. Hosted supports our streaming + tool call orchestration out of the box. On Dedicated/Private, the orchestration runs in your environment and we can plug into your connectors — you'll want the SE deep-dive to map auth flow and callback URLs. Also watch for callback latency if your APIs sit in a private VPC.
[04:05] Priya: About cost — how much more expensive is Dedicated initially?
[04:09] Jasmine: There's an uplift because you reserve capacity; price depends on committed throughput. We usually see higher fixed cost but lower unit cost at volume. We'll send a ballpark based on expected qps and token volume.
[04:21] Dina: We have a rough monthly token budget — expect 200M tokens for the pilot. Does that change recommendations?
[04:28] Marco: 200M is substantive. With that volume Dedicated often becomes attractive for cost predictability. But for the POC we can do hosted to iterate quickly and then transition to Dedicated for production.
[04:38] Markus: For our evaluation, we want: latency and perplexity-like metrics on summarization, multilingual accuracy, and hallucination checks. Also need a way to measure prompt stability.
[04:48] Marco: Totally. We have an evaluation harness we can run against your sample corpus; it'll produce latency percentiles (p50/p95), token counts, and a QA-style hallucination check. We'll need the sample docs.
[04:59] Priya: We'll try to upload a redacted sample set, maybe 30–50k docs. Is there a recommended size?
[05:05] Marco: 5–10k representative docs is usually enough to profile, but we can scale. Also helpful: typical queries and session traces.
[05:12] Dina: On encryption — do you support customer-managed KMS?
[05:16] Jasmine: Yes. Dedicated and Private integrate with customer KMS; Hosted can use Redwood-managed keys but we also offer Bring-Your-Own-Key for certain enterprise tiers. We'll send specifics in the security pack.
[05:27] Markus: Regarding caching — you mentioned KV cache earlier — how does that work with long-doc RAG?
[05:32] Marco: We do prefix/KV caching primarily for autoregressive generation to reduce repeated token compute in iterative sessions. For RAG, the retrieval layer reduces input size by selecting top chunks; caching helps when users iteratively explore similar query contexts. It doesn't replace retrieval, but it's complementary.
[05:47] Priya: Suppose we have a workflow: user enters query, system retrieves 30 chunks, model generates answer + calls an approvals API if flagged. We need the ability to orchestrate a tool call mid-generation?
[05:58] Marco: Tool-calling supports synchronous and asynchronous patterns. If you need a mid-generation external call, we typically wire that as a pre-check or post-check; in some flows we do function-calling style where the model returns structured payload that triggers your backend. We can demo both.
[06:12] Dina: We have strict PII handling — do you have redaction tooling or middleware?
[06:16] Marco: We offer integration patterns: pre-ingest PII redaction, prompt-time filters, and post-generation scrubbing. For strict customers, pre-ingest redaction plus Private deployment is typical.
[06:26] Markus: A technical q on quantization: how stable are 4-bit runtimes for long context? we've seen regression on reasoning tasks.
[06:33] Marco: Good point — 4-bit quant can impact numeric stability on some tasks. For summarization we recommend testing both 8-bit and 4-bit; Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per model and workload. We'll include recommended profiles in the perf notes.
[06:48] Priya: What about multi-turn sessions with context window growth? We sometimes have follow-up queries referencing prior chat.
[06:55] Marco: For multi-turn we rely on session management and KV caches. You can also store condensed conversation state to reduce prompt size. For very long windows, you can use progressive summarization to keep tokens bounded.
[07:08] Dina: Any red flags on GDPR/data residency? Some of our EU customers require data stays in EU.
[07:14] Jasmine: We have EU regions for hosted, and Dedicated/Private allows you to control region and residency. We also provide data processing addenda. We'll include that in the security pack.
[07:25] Markus: On benchmarking, can you run p50/p95 latency for 32k vs 64k contexts? those will be very different numbers.
[07:31] Marco: Yep, we'll run both. For 64k the p95 can increase substantially; we'll provide absolute numbers and a cost estimate. For some workloads, chunked retrieval plus a short-generation model yields better latency-cost tradeoffs than a single long-context pass.
[07:47] Priya: Hmm, that's interesting — chunk + synthesize vs full ingest. We'll want a comparison.
[07:52] Marco: We'll include both approaches in the evaluation.
[07:55] Markus: Regarding connectors — we use a proprietary document DB behind auth. We need secure connectors.
[07:59] Marco: On Dedicated/Private we can deploy connectors inside your network or use a connector adapter with mutual TLS. We'll map details in the SE deep-dive.
[08:11] Dina: Who handles model upgrades and rollouts? If we pin a model and then Redwood updates the runtime, how does that affect us?
[08:18] Jasmine: Customers can pin model versions and choose rollout policies. Our Console allows canary/rollout configs. We'll work with you on a controlled rollout plan.
[08:26] Priya: About eval metrics — do you provide automated hallucination scoring?
[08:30] Marco: We provide QA-based checks and entailment heuristics; it's not perfect but useful to catch regressions across models. We also alert on quality regressions tied to prompt sets in Redwood Optimize.
[08:43] Dina: Ok sounds good. Let's talk timeline — we want a POC within the quarter. Is that feasible?
[08:48] Jasmine: Yes. Quick plan: week 1: security docs + sample data sharing; week 2: Redwood runs initial bench on hosted with your sample; week 3: joint deep-dive to map connectors; weeks 4–8: POC run with success metrics. We can condense if needed.
[09:03] Priya: Budget? we'll need a rough SOW.
[09:06] Jasmine: We'll put together a 3-month POC SOW with hosted consumption estimate and an alternate Dedicated quote.
[09:12] Markus: Any immediate blockers for us to get started?
[09:15] Marco: Just sample data and a contact for your infra team. Also an NDA if required — we can handle that.
[09:21] Dina: We'll send the sample corpus and infra contact.
[09:24] Jasmine: Great. Quick demo offer — do you want a short walkthrough of Redwood Console and model selection now or save for deep-dive?
[09:31] Priya: Maybe a 15-min quick look now if time.
[09:34] Jasmine: Sure — Marco, do a quick share.
[09:37] [SCREEN SHARE START]
[09:38] Marco: Alright, this is the Console — per-route dashboards, model catalog, perf profiles. Here you can see model latency p95 precomputed for different sequence lengths — this is synthetic but helpful. Also our rollout controls. Bear with the demo slowness — wifi, lol.
[09:57] Priya: Looks straightforward. How do we request a sandbox project?
[10:01] Jasmine: We'll provision keys and a sandbox org — I'll follow up.
[10:05] Marco: A couple more technical notes: for long context we sometimes recommend chunking into ~4k chunks and using a synth step; also consider retrieval with semantic embeddings — we support embeddings in multiple dims and can route that to vector DBs.
[10:20] Markus: Which vector DBs do you commonly integrate with?
[10:23] Marco: We have connectors to Pinecone, Milvus, and we support pushing vectors to S3-based stores via our adapters. If you have something homegrown we can do a connector.
[10:32] Dina: Any legal procurement hoops — we have standard contracts.
[10:35] Jasmine: We'll send templates. For enterprise customers we do custom SOW/terms.
[10:40] Priya: For the POC success metrics: accuracy on QA, latency p95 under X for short answers, and hallucination rate under Y. We'll formalize and share.
[10:49] Jasmine: Perfect. We'll pair with you to finalize metrics.
[10:52] [00:10:52] Dina: Are there known regressions for Mistral on long German legal text?
[10:58] Marco: There's some variability; that's exactly why we run model-specific tests on your corpus.
[11:02] Markus: Ok. Last question — can Redwood host a model tuned by us (customer fine-tune) on Dedicated?
[11:08] Marco: Yes, Dedicated supports hosting customer-finetuned artifacts — we manage versioning and rollouts. If you want to keep artifacts on-prem we can do that on Private deployments.
[11:18] Dina: Great. I think that's all from our side for now.
[11:21] Jasmine: Thanks everyone. Recap of immediate next steps is: security docs + SOC2, perf bench for 32k/64k, sandbox keys, and schedule deep-dive. I'll send calendar invites.
[11:35] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[11:37] [END]
